passages.original: numquidnam et sanctus Ambrosius nuptiarum bonitatem ac non potius istorum haereticorum quamuis tunc nondum adparentium uanitatem huius suae sententiae ueritate damnauit? quod ideo commemorandum putaui, quia Pelagius sic laudat Ambrosium, ut dicat: \'beatus Ambrosius episcopus, in cuius praecipue libris Romana elucet fides, qui scriptorum inter Latinos flos quidam speciosus enituit, cuius fidem et purissimum in scripturis sensum ne inimicus quidem ausus est reprehendere\'.
passages.english: Surely holy Ambrose did not, by the truth of this statement of his, condemn the goodness of marriage, but rather the emptiness of these heretics, although they had not yet appeared at that time? I thought this worth mentioning because Pelagius praises Ambrose in such terms as to say: 'The blessed bishop Ambrose, in whose books above all the Roman faith shines forth, who stood out among the Latin writers as a kind of beautiful flower, whose faith and most pure understanding of the Scriptures not even an enemy has dared to criticize.'

passages.original: aut si et illum fidelissimum uirum hoc secundum Manicheos sapuisse iactatis, iactate, iactate, ut mensuram Iouiniani perfectius inpleatis; nos cum illo homine dei patienter uestra maledicta et conuicia sustinemus. et tamen haeresiarches uester Pelagius fidem et purissimum in scripturis sensum sic laudat Ambrosii, ut dicat ne inimicum quidem ausum esse reprehendere. quo ergo progressi fueritis adtendite et uos ab ausibus Iouiniani tandem aliquando cohibete. quamuis ille nimis laudando nuptias sanctae illas uirginitati adaequauit et tamen nuptiarum fructibus ab utero etiam recentibus Christum saluatorem et de potestate diaboli redemptorem necessarium non negauit: quod uos negatis et, quia uobis pro eorum salute, qui nondum pro se loqui possunt, et pro fidei catholicae fundamentis resistimus, Manicheos nos esse iactatis.
passages.english: Or if you boast that that most faithful man too held this view in the manner of the Manichees, boast it, boast it, so that you may more completely fill up the measure of Jovinian; we, together with that man of God, patiently endure your curses and insults. And yet your heresiarch Pelagius so praises the faith of Ambrose and his most pure understanding of the scriptures as to say that not even an enemy has dared to find fault with him. Consider, then, how far you have advanced, and at long last restrain yourselves from the audacities of Jovinian. Although he, by praising marriage too much, made it equal to holy virginity, he nevertheless did not deny that Christ the Saviour and Redeemer from the power of the devil is necessary for the fruits of marriage, even those fresh from the womb. This you deny, and because we resist you on behalf of the salvation of those who cannot yet speak for themselves, and on behalf of the foundations of the catholic faith, you boast that we are Manichees.
passages.notes: 'That most faithful man' and 'that man of God' refer to Ambrose, quoted in the preceding context. 'Iactatis' is rendered 'boast'; it may also carry the sense 'loudly assert' or 'bandy about'.

passages.original: in uno homine iure uituperatur intentio et natura laudatur, quia duo sunt, quae contrariis adplicentur; sed etiam in paruulo non unum est tantum, id est natura, in qua creatus est homo a deo bono; habet enim et uitium, quod per unum in omnes homines pertransiit, sicut sapit apostolus, non sicut desipit Pelagius uel Caelestius uel eorum quicumque discipulus. horum itaque duorum, quae in paruulo esse diximus, unum adscribitur deo, alterum diabolo. et quod utrumque propter unum horum, id est propter uitium subicitur potestati diaboli, ideo non est incongruum, quia non fit ipsius diaboli potestate, sed dei;
passages.english: In one adult human being the intention is rightly blamed and the nature praised, because there are two things there, to which contrary [judgements] may be applied; but even in an infant there is not only one thing, that is, the nature in which man was created by the good God; for it also has the fault which passed through one man into all men, as the apostle wisely holds, not as Pelagius or Caelestius or any disciple of theirs foolishly holds. Of these two things, then, which we have said are in the infant, one is ascribed to God, the other to the devil. And that both, on account of one of them, that is, on account of the fault, are made subject to the power of the devil, is therefore not unfitting, because this happens not by the power of the devil himself but by that of God;
passages.notes: 'In uno homine' here evidently means an adult with will, contrasted with the infant who has no will (cf. context).

passages.original: Sed, ut dixi, sentiat de ista libidine iste quodlibet, praedicet utlibet, laudet quantumlibet — sicut enim multis locis significat, multum libet — ut eius si non usibus, saltem laudibus Pelagiani oblectentur, quicumque eorum proposito continentiae carne coniugum non fruuntur, tantum paruulis parcat, ut non eos laudet inutiliter defendatque crudeliter, saluos esse non dicat, non ad laudatorem Pelagium, sed ad saluatorem Christum uenire permittat. nam ut iam liber iste claudatur, quoniam ita sermo illius terminatus est, qui in chartula quam misisti scriptus est, ut diceret: \'uere credito quia per Iesum facta sunt omnia, et sine ipso factum est nihi' ?
passages.english: But, as I said, let this man think what he likes about this lust, proclaim it as he likes, praise it as much as he likes — for, as he indicates in many places, he likes it very much — so that the Pelagians, those of them who by a resolve of continence do not enjoy the flesh of spouses, may be delighted, if not by its use, at least by its praises; only let him spare the little ones, so that he does not praise them uselessly and defend them cruelly, does not say they are saved, [but] allows them to come not to Pelagius their praiser but to Christ their Saviour. For now, to close this book: since his discourse, which was written in the little paper you sent, ended by saying: 'Truly believe that all things were made through Jesus, and without him nothing was made'
passages.notes: 'nihi' ?' is a scanning error for 'nihil'; the sentence continues in the following context.
